_comment: Identity -> permission, for requests arriving through .claude/commands/route.md. Answers two questions and no others: WHO is asking (requester_id), and WHAT may they reach (tier + departments). Consumed by route.md only. This is not an authentication system — the channel is responsible for proving identity before it hands a request over; this file only says what a proven identity is allowed to do.
_maintenance: Adding a person is one entry here plus one channel identifier. A channel identifier that resolves to no entry is REFUSED, never downgraded to staff and never guessed — see resolution.unknown_identifier below. When a staff member leaves, delete the entry; do not set tier to null, which reads as a malformed entry rather than a revocation.
_privacy_note: THIS REPO IS PUBLIC (see CLAUDE.md 'Open items', settled 2026-07-26). Never put a real phone number, personal email address, or WhatsApp handle in this file. Channel identifiers are stored as sha256(REQUESTER_ID_SALT + raw_identifier), hex, first 16 chars. The salt lives in .env (REQUESTER_ID_SALT) and never in the repo. The alternative, equally acceptable: have Make resolve the raw identifier to an opaque requester_id before the request ever reaches this system, in which case the channels[] list here stays empty and Make owns the mapping.

admin._comment: Albert, and anyone he explicitly grants the same reach. Sees everything, including items whose sensitivity is `private`.

staff._comment: Titan staff. May reach the operational departments and sees only `team`-sensitivity items. This is the tier a WhatsApp number would land in.

requesters._note: The `chat` and `command` channels are the local session, which is already Albert's by definition — a cloud session runs under his account. The `routine` channel is every scheduled Routine, which he owns. These three are the only wildcards in this file and they are all the same person.

resolution._comment: How route.md turns a channel identifier into a tier. Fail-closed at every step — the same posture as the notion_task_eligible_mailboxes exclusion in contracts/notion-task-schema.md, which is a hard rule precisely because a wrong answer misfiles something private.
order: hash the raw identifier: sha256(REQUESTER_ID_SALT + raw)[:16]
find the requesters[] entry whose channels[] contains that (channel, identifier) pair
read its tier; read that tier's may_see_private and departments from tiers{}
resolution.unknown_identifier: REFUSE. Reply that the sender is not registered and stop. Do not default to staff, do not answer 'just the safe parts', and do not ask the sender who they are — an unregistered identity answering that question is not evidence.
resolution.unknown_tier: REFUSE. A requesters[] entry naming a tier that tiers{} does not define is a malformed registry, not a permission question.
resolution.department_not_allowed: Reply that the department is out of reach for this requester and name which departments are in reach. Do not silently reroute to general — a staff member asking Finance a question should learn they cannot, not receive a General answer that looks like the answer.
resolution.private_filter: An item whose effective sensitivity is `private` is NEVER returned to a requester whose tier has may_see_private: false. This is a filter applied at reply time, not a new routing axis: the item's sensitivity was already set at ingest per contracts/ingest-schema.md and defaulted per source in notion-destinations.json. Filtering happens after the department has done its work, so a lead's plan file on disk is unchanged by who asked.
